aspects.says: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE makes a second locking read of the row wait until the first transaction ends, and then return the committed value.
basis: section:SELECT ... FOR UPDATE Makes the Second Reader Wait for the First Commit

aspects.says: On H2, READ COMMITTED shows non-repeatable reads, phantoms and lost updates, while REPEATABLE READ reads a snapshot and refuses the second writer of a changed row with SQLState 40001.
basis: section:An Isolation Level Is What Your Database Does, and on H2 None Stops Write Skew

aspects.says: On H2, SERIALIZABLE let write skew through when two transactions read the same rows and wrote different ones.
basis: section:An Isolation Level Is What Your Database Does, and on H2 None Stops Write Skew

aspects.says: A row lock lasts until commit() or rollback(), so a code path that returns without either keeps other transactions waiting.
basis: section:SELECT ... FOR UPDATE Makes the Second Reader Wait for the First Commit

aspects.says: Under READ COMMITTED, reading a value, computing the new one in Java and writing it back loses a concurrent update, and a lock inside one JVM does not stop another instance.
basis: section:Read, Compute in Java, Write Back Loses an Update Under READ COMMITTED

aspects.says: When the new value is a function of the old one, a single UPDATE such as balance = balance + ? waits on the row lock and adds to the committed value.
basis: section:Read, Compute in Java, Write Back Loses an Update Under READ COMMITTED
aspects.reason: the practices cover the read-modify-write that needs Java logic between the read and the write; the one-statement form is shown by the run and leaves the reader nothing to decide

aspects.says: A version-checked UPDATE still waits on another writer's uncommitted change of the row, and then returns 0.
basis: section:A Version Column Turns a Lost Update into an Update Count of 0

aspects.says: After SQLState 40001 the transaction is gone, so it is retried from its first statement, and failures that a retry cannot fix are not retried.
basis: section:On H2, a Lock Timeout Fails One Statement; a Deadlock Rolls Back the Whole Transaction

aspects.says: rollback(savepoint) undoes everything after the savepoint and keeps the transaction open, so a savepoint at the start of each group of statements drops a bad group whole.
basis: section:A Failed Statement Undoes Only Itself; a Savepoint Undoes the Group

aspects.says: On H2 a failed statement undoes only itself: the transaction stays open, and a later commit keeps the statements before it.
basis: section:A Failed Statement Undoes Only Itself; a Savepoint Undoes the Group

aspects.says: On H2, a lock timeout (HYT00) fails one statement and leaves the transaction open, while a deadlock (40001) rolls the whole transaction back.
basis: section:On H2, a Lock Timeout Fails One Statement; a Deadlock Rolls Back the Whole Transaction

aspects.says: A version-checked UPDATE returns an update count of 0 when another writer saved first; the caller reads again before retrying, and every writer increments the version.
basis: section:A Version Column Turns a Lost Update into an Update Count of 0
